plastic_pet.name: PET plastic (1)
plastic_pet.summary: Clear bottles and food containers, such as water and soft-drink bottles.
steps: Empty the container completely
Rinse it and let it drain
Put the cap back on
Flatten it if possible, then place it in the plastics bin

plastic_hdpe.name: HDPE plastic (2)
plastic_hdpe.summary: Milk jugs, detergent and shampoo bottles, and thick opaque containers.
steps: Empty the container
Rinse out any leftover contents
Leave the cap on
Place it in the plastics bin

plastic_pvc.name: PVC plastic (3)
plastic_pvc.summary: Pipes, some packaging, blister trays and some bottles.
steps: Check your local rules first, because PVC is often not accepted
Empty and rinse it if it was a container
If it is not accepted, put it in general waste
Never burn it

plastic_ldpe.name: LDPE plastic (4)
plastic_ldpe.summary: Plastic bags, films and squeezable bottles.
steps: Shake out the contents and keep it clean and dry
Collect clean bags and film together inside one bag
Take them to a film-plastic drop-off if one exists, instead of mixing them loose with other plastics
Otherwise put them in general waste

plastic_pp.name: PP plastic (5)
plastic_pp.summary: Yogurt tubs, bottle caps, food containers and straws.
steps: Empty the container and scrape out food
Rinse it
Place it in the plastics bin
Keep the lid with the container if your collector accepts it

plastic_ps.name: PS plastic (6)
plastic_ps.summary: Foam trays, disposable cups and rigid clear packaging.
steps: Empty it and wipe it clean
Check your local rules, because PS is often not accepted
Put crumbling foam in a bag before disposal
If it is not accepted, use general waste

plastic_other.name: Other plastic (7)
plastic_other.summary: Mixed or unlabeled plastics, such as some bottles, discs and composite packaging.
steps: Read the label or check your local rules
Empty and rinse it
If it is not accepted, put it in general waste
Reuse it where possible

plastic_unknown.name: Plastic (type unknown)
plastic_unknown.summary: A plastic item whose type could not be identified.
steps: Look for the number inside the triangle symbol
Empty it and rinse it
Place it in the plastics bin if your collector takes mixed plastics
If you are not sure, use general waste

paper.name: Paper
paper.summary: Office paper, newspapers, magazines and clean paper bags.
steps: Keep it dry and clean
Remove plastic covers, clips and staples if that is easy
Stack it flat
Greasy or food-soiled paper goes in general waste

cardboard.name: Cardboard
steps: Remove tape, labels and plastic fillers
Flatten the box
Keep it dry
Greasy parts, such as a pizza box lid, go in general waste

carton_beverage.name: Beverage carton
steps: Empty the carton
Rinse it and let it dry
Flatten it and keep the cap on
Place it in the paper or carton bin if your area accepts cartons

glass.name: Glass
steps: Empty and rinse them
Remove the lids
Do not add ceramics, mirrors, window glass or light bulbs
Place them in the glass bin
warnings: Wrap broken glass in thick paper and mark the package before disposal to protect collectors.

metal_aluminum.name: Aluminum
metal_aluminum.summary: Drink cans, foil and food trays.
steps: Empty and rinse cans
Crush them if your collector allows it
Scrunch clean foil into a ball
Place them in the metals bin

metal_steel.name: Steel
metal_steel.summary: Food cans, tins and metal lids.
steps: Empty and rinse the can
Press any sharp lid edge inward
Place it in the metals bin
warnings: The cut edges of opened cans are sharp. Handle them with care.

metal_other.name: Other metal
metal_other.summary: Scrap metal such as tools, pipes, pans and metal parts.
steps: Remove any non-metal parts
Keep scrap apart from household recycling
Take it to a scrap metal collector or collection point
Sell it as scrap if it has value

organic_food.name: Food waste
organic_food.summary: Leftovers, peels, coffee grounds and spoiled food.
steps: Remove packaging and plastic
Drain excess liquid
Place it in the organic or compost bin
Keep cooking oil out of it

organic_garden.name: Garden waste
organic_garden.summary: Leaves, grass clippings, small branches and plants.
steps: Remove stones, plastic and treated wood
Cut branches short and tie them in bundles
Compost it or use the garden-waste collection

ewaste_small.name: Small electronics
ewaste_small.summary: Phones, chargers, cables, headphones and small gadgets.
steps: Never put them in general trash
Remove the batteries if you can do so easily and safely
Delete your personal data from the device
Take them to an e-waste collection point
warnings: Electronics contain hazardous materials. Never put them in general waste.
This is guidance only. Check with your local authorities for collection points.

ewaste_large.name: Large appliances
ewaste_large.summary: Fridges, washing machines, TVs and computers.
steps: Never put them out with general trash
Unplug and empty the appliance
Keep it intact and do not break it open
Ask the seller to take it back, or call a specialist collector
warnings: Fridges and air conditioners contain gases that harm the environment. Do not break the pipes.
This is guidance only. Check with your local authorities for collection options.

battery.name: Battery
steps: Do not throw it in general waste
Tape over the terminals with clear tape
Store it dry and away from metal objects
Take it to a battery collection point
warnings: Damaged, swollen or leaking batteries can overheat or catch fire. Do not crush, pierce or open them.
This is guidance only. Check with your local authorities for collection points.

textile.name: Textiles
steps: Donate items that are still wearable
Wash them and let them dry
Tie worn-out items in a bag
Take them to a textile recycling point
Wet or moldy textiles go in general waste

hazardous_chemical.name: Hazardous chemicals
hazardous_chemical.summary: Paint, solvents, pesticides, cleaning chemicals and used oils.
steps: Keep the product in its original labeled container
Never mix different chemicals
Never pour it down a drain or onto the ground
Take it to a hazardous waste collection point
warnings: Many chemicals are toxic, flammable or corrosive. Keep them away from children, heat and flames.
Never pour chemicals into drains or soil.
This is guidance only. Check with your local authorities for hazardous waste collection.

medical.name: Medical waste
medical.summary: Needles and syringes, expired medication, masks and dressings.
steps: Put needles and sharps in a rigid, puncture-proof container with a lid
Return unused or expired medication to a pharmacy
Seal used masks and dressings in a bag before disposal
Do not recap or bend needles
warnings: Needles can cause injuries and spread infection. Never put loose sharps in a bag or bin.
Do not flush medication or throw it in general waste.
This is guidance only. Check with your local health or waste authority.

wood.name: Wood
wood.summary: Pallets, furniture offcuts and untreated timber.
steps: Remove nails, screws and metal parts
Reuse or donate pieces that are still usable
Keep treated or painted wood separate
Take it to a wood collection point
warnings: Painted or treated wood can release harmful chemicals if burned.

construction.name: Construction waste
construction.summary: Rubble, concrete, tiles, bricks and plaster.
steps: Keep it separate from household waste
Remove metal, wood and plastic
Take it to a construction-waste site or arrange a collection
Reuse clean rubble where possible
warnings: Old insulation, roofing or pipes may contain asbestos. Do not break them and ask your local authorities.
Wear gloves and lift heavy loads safely.

general_residual.name: General residual waste
general_residual.summary: Waste that cannot be recycled or composted, such as dirty wrappers, ceramics and used tissues.
steps: Use this only as a last option
Check that the item cannot be reused or recycled
Tie it securely in a bag
Place it in the general waste bin
